thread:
Jules (Design): thinking out loud: what about a 'quarantine' fallback mode? Instead of visible degrade, traffic stays routed to a safe, limited variant while we gather contextual traces. The user experience is unchanged but ops get a dedicated audit feed.
Evan (Backend): idea makes sense. Two main pieces: 1) routing layer flag to send X% to quarantine variant, 2) structured audit events with reason + input hash.
Priya (SRE): must be able to opt into noisy vs quiet quarantine. Quiet = no pages, noisy = page. Also want an automatic severity bump if quarantined requests correlate with error spikes elsewhere.
Noah (Product): product framing: quarantine helps reduce user-visible regressions while we triage. UX should show 'Quarantine active' with the % diverted and a quick reason (e.g., model OOM, high latency).
DeployBot: [deploy] rollout/2026-04-06T14:40 initiated by @noah
Jules (Design): UI mock: tiny pill "Quarantine: 12%" + hover shows last 5 reasons and a 'preview recent samples' button. Also add an affordance to change sample capture rate inline.
Evan (Backend): propose config shape (simple JSON) for rollout record:

```
{
  "fallback":{
    "strategy":"quarantine",    // quarantine | mirror | fallback_variant
    "divert_fraction":0.12,
    "capture_rate":0.05,         // full payload capture fraction
    "escalation":{
      "threshold_pct":3,
      "window_sec":600
    }
  }
}
```

That should cover most cases.
Priya (SRE): add field: "escalation_on_related_errors": true. If quarantine correlates with downstream 500s we should escalate earlier.
Ibrahim (Billing): we need to mark quarantined traffic for chargeback. Even if user doesn't see degrade, the compute cost differs. Tag events with billing_code=quarantine.
Kara (Legal): capture_rate and payload capture need PII redaction controls per org region. Also provide a way to opt-out of sample capture for specific customers.
Tess (Support): Support wants a compact link that opens the last sampled request (redacted) when troubleshooting. Also permissioned view for customer-facing agents.
Noah (Product): question: should quarantine be reversible with a single click (abort quarantine) or should we require a rollout rollback?
Evan (Backend): safe to have both: a fast 'abort quarantine' that stops diversion, and a full rollback action that also steps back model versions. Abort should be logged and audited.
Jules (Design): add microcopy: "Quarantine silently isolates a subset of traffic to a safe variant while we collect telemetry. Quarantine does not surface errors to users by default." Good?
Priya (SRE): add operational metrics: `quarantine_diverted_count`, `quarantine_failure_rate`, `quarantine_latency_p50/p95`. We should also emit tags for suspect-reason to help query.
Evan (Backend): agreed. Also an event stream schema: [timestamp, rollout_id, diverted, reason, variant_from, variant_to, trace_id]. Keep it compact to save storage.
Ibrahim (Billing): Also need an aggregated daily report of quarantined token-usage per customer for billing reconciliation.
Kara (Legal): retention policy: standard audit retention 90 days by default; enterprise customers can set longer. And document how to request export/deletion for GDPR.
Noah (Product): decision items: 1) support quarantine strategy and UI pill, 2) config schema + abort action + audit logs, 3) capture-rate and PII redaction knobs, 4) billing tagging and reports, 5) escalation rule correlation. Any blockers?
Evan (Backend): will prototype API and minimal telemetry emitter.
Jules (Design): will put mocks in #design and include the abort/rollback CTA states.
Priya (SRE): I'll write SLO notes on when to trigger automatic escalation.
Tess (Support): please add a short FAQ blurb for Support playbook.
DeployBot: [info] audit_stream: quarantine/1759870001 created
Noah (Product): thanks team, we'll sync next week to review prototype.
